 JUDGMENT
As the controversy involved in these First Appeals is identical, therefore, they are being disposed of by this common judgment.
For the sake of convenience, the facts narrated in F.A. No. 778/2020 (Land Acquisition Officer & another V/s. Keshrichandra S/o. Panchilal & others) are being taken into consideration.

01. The Land Acquisition Officer, Sardar Sarovar Project, Dharampuri, District Dhar has filed these bunch of first appeals against the judgment and Award dated 2.4.2018 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Dharampuri, District Dhar in Land - : 21 :-

19 Acquisition Case No. 1191/2013 whereby the compensation has been enhanced by awarding @ Rs. 8.00 Lakhs per Hectare for irrigated land situated in Village Pandhranya, Tehsil Dharampuri, District Dhar.

The facts of the case, in short, are as under :
02.

The Executive Engineer, OSP Canal Division, Dhamnod, District Dhar vide letter dated 26.8.2008 requested the Land Acquisition Officer to acquire the private lands admeasuring 23.668 Hectare of Village Pandhranya for completion of the third Phase of the canal under Omkareshwar Project.

In pursuant to the aforesaid request, a Notification u/s. 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act was issued on 19.9.2008 and published in two Hindi newspaper viz. Swadesh and in Dainik Bhaskar on 24.9.2008.
Thereafter, Notification u/s. 6 of the Land Acquisition Act was issued on 17.10.2008 and published in Hindi daily newspaper Dainik Bhaskar and Nai Dunia on 16.10.2008.

Thereafter, the Collector and Ex-officio Dy. Secretary, State of M.P., Dhar vide order dated 12.11.2008 granted permission of acquisition u/s. 7 of the Land Acquisition Act for issuance of Notification u/s. 9 of the Act.

Vide Notification u/s. 9 dated 7.1.2009 the Land Acquisition Officer initiated the proceedings for deciding the compensation for acquisition in all the three phases i.e. Phase No. 1, 2 and 3 of the Canal of Omkareshwar Project.
All the landowners appeared before the Land Acquisition Officer and submitted as many as 35 objections.
For those landowners who agreed to receive 80% of the amount, the same was paid to them.
03. The State Government vide circular dated 16.4.1991 issued directions to pay the compensation uniformly in respect to the land which is close to the irrigation command area.

The Land Acquisition - : 22 :-
F.A. No. 777/2020 & connected appeals.

Officer after considering all the circulars issued by the State Government and the guidelines issued by the Collector of the concerned village and objections of the landowners, vide award dated 28.5.2009 decided to grant the compensation for irrigated lands @ Rs.3,30,000/- per Hectare and for un-irrigated lands @
Rs.2,10,000/- along with solecium @ 30% and interest @ 12% per annum.
04. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid award, the land owners sought reference from the Collector u/s. 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, which was referred to the District Judge for adjudication.
The land owners produced two sale-deeds of sale of land situated at Village Gyaspur Khedi @ Rs.5.00 Lakhs per Hectare as an exmplers and also exhibited the map to show the location of their village.
The land owners examined themselves and in rebuttal, the Patwari of Halka No.11 was examined by the NVDA.

After appreciating the evidence that came on record especially relying on two sale-deeds of Village Gyaspur Khedi, the learned Additional District Judge, Dharampuri vide award dated 2.4.2018 enhanced the amount of compensation for the irrigated land @ Rs.8.00 Lakhs per Hectare.

07. The Land Acquisition Officer has also filed the First Appeals No. 777/2020, 778/2020,
779/2020, 780/2020, 781/2020, 782/2020, 784/220, 786/2020, 787/2020, 788/2020, 789/2020,

Rs.8.00 Lakhs has wrongly been awarded without there being any evidence on record.

08. Shri Vivek Patwa, learned counsel appearing for the Land Acquisition Officer/ NVDA, submitted the coordinate bench hurriedly decided the First Appeals without calling the records and without connecting these First Appeals filed by the Land Acquisition Officer /NVDA hence review petitions have been filed.

It is further submitted by the learned counsel that in Para 23 of the award, the learned Additional District Judge while relying on the sale deeds of a nearby village has held that the compensation at the rate of Rs.5.0 Lakhs per Hectare for irrigated land is proper but in Para 26 of the award without assigning any reason has awarded the amount of compensation @ Rs.8.00 Lakhs per Hectare of irrigated land and Rs.7.00 Lakhs for un- irrigated land.

It is further submitted by the learned counsel that the landowners did not exhibit any sale deed of the Village Pandhranya, the sale deeds of nearby village have wrongly relied on, hence the - : 24 :-
F.A. No. 777/2020 & connected appeals.

impugned award passed by the learned Additional District Judge is liable to be set aside and award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer be maintained.

sentences.text: Shri A.S. Garg, learned senior counsel appearing for the land owners, argued that so far as review petitions are concerned, they are liable to be dismissed because the judgment dated 11.5.2020 was passed by this court way of consent given by the learned Govt.

Advocate, therefore,
such a consented order is not liable to be reviewed and the review petitions are liable to be dismissed.

It is further submitted that in the case of Devdutt (supra), this Court did not disturb the amount of compensation assessed by the reference court but reduced the percentage development cost from 65% to one-third relying on the judgment of the Apex Court.

In the case of Devdutt (supra), the compensation was awarded @ Rs.13,88,889/- per Hectare, but in the present case, the compensation has been awarded only @ Rs.8.00 Lakhs per Hectare, whereas both the villages viz.
Gyaspur Khedi and Pandhranya are adjacent to each other.
10. Since all the First Appeals and Review Petitions arise out of a common award and a common issue is involved, therefore, the same are heard and decided analogously.

11. So far as the scope of review is concerned, if the mistake is apparent on the face of the record,
even if the order is passed by way of consent, the same is liable to be reviewed.
It is settled law
that the consent given by the lawyer is not binding on the parties if it is contrary to the facts and law.

Therefore, even if the order/judgment dated 11.5.2020 has been passed with the consent of the Government Advocate and if it is not in accordance with the law and there is a - : 25 :-
F.A. No. 777/2020 & connected appeals.
mistake apparent on the face of the record, the review petitions are maintainable.
Even otherwise, there are other first appeals filed by NVDA challenging the same award passed by the Additional District Judge, hence, all these issues are liable to be decided on merit.
Hence, the appeals which have been decided by judgment dated 11.5.2020 are liable to be reconsidered on merit.

Moreso, the first appeals, in which,
review petitions are filed, were decided on the very first day of their listing, without the records of the reference court and the Land Acquisition Officer.

The learned Govt.
Advocate had no occasion to consult the Officer-in-Chair of the case and without obtaining any instructions as to whether the Land Acquisition Officer is going to challenge the award or not, the learned Govt. The Govt. Advocate ought not to have given consent on the very first day of hearing of the appeals for final disposal.

Hence,
the review petitions are liable to be entertained, and all facts and grounds are liable to be reconsidered along with connected First Appeals.
Appreciations & Conclusion 12.
In these present cases, the acquired land in question is situated in Village Pandhranya needed for the completion of the third phase of the canal of the Omkareshwar Project.

For Phase 1 and 2 of the Project, the agricultural lands of other nearby villages were also acquired by issuing separate notifications under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 , at the relevant point of time i.e. in the year Sardar Sarovar Project vs Kalu on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4642154/
22 2008.

In the case, Devdutt (supra) the land of Gyaspur Khedi was acquired for which the compensation @ Rs.13,88,889/- was awarded for irrigated land and against which F.A.
No.1314/2014 was filed and the same had been decided to vide judgment dated 30.11.2017 and the said judgment has - : 26 :-
F.A. No. 777/2020 & connected appeals.
not been challenged by the Land Acquisition Officer and it has attained finality.

12. So far as the present cases are concerned, the learned Additional District Judge for awarding the compensation @ Rs.8.00 Lakhs per Hectare for irrigated land after discussion in Para 23 of the judgment about the sale-deeds vide Exh. P/1. Vide Exh.
P/1 out of the land bearing Survey No. 49 area measuring 0.126 Hectares was sold for Rs.5.00 Lakhs in the same year in which the notification u/s. 4 of the Land Acquisition Act was issued.

All these villages viz. Guljhari, Dhamnod, Vikhron,
Pandhranya and Gyaspur Khedi are adjacent to each other and the purpose of the acquisition order dated the land is the same i.e. construction of the canal, hence the sale-deed of the nearby village can be taken as an exemplar because all the lands are agricultural and are going to get the benefit of irrigation from the water in the canal.

Therefore, the learned Additional District Judge has not committed any error while taking into consideration the sale deeds of a nearby village when no sale deeds were available of the Village Pandhranya.
13.
In defence, the concerned Patwari has not produced any sale deed of Villae Pandhranya.

On the contrary, in the cross-examination, he has admitted that the agriculture land of Gram Guljhari, Dhamnod, Vikhron and Pandhranya are of the same nature and as per circular dated 16.4.1991 same criteria is liable to be adopted for the grant of compensation uniformly for the land situated at nearby command area.

Therefore, as compared to compensation awarded in the case of Devdutt (supra) @ Rs.13,88,889/-,
the compensation of Rs.8.00 Lakhs in the present case cannot be said to be on the higher side.

Hence, no - : 27 :-
F.A. No. 777/2020 & connected appeals.

interference is called for and no enhancement is liable to be made as the land owners have already accepted the same at the time of disposal of the first appeals vide judgment dated 11.5.2020.
Sardar Sarovar Project vs Kalu on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4642154/
23 14.
Now, the only issue which requires consideration by this Court is about the appropriate percentage to be applied.
The bunch of First Appeals in the first round were allowed by applying the judgment passed in the case of Devdutt (supra).

Para 6,
7 and 8 of the aforesaid judgment are reproduced below :

"6. On due consideration of the aforesaid so also in the absence of any material, I relying on para-16 of the decision of Apex Court in the case of Sabhia Mohammed Yusuf Abdul Hamid Mulla (Dead) by LRs. & others (supra) direct the respondents to deduct 1/3rd towards development charges.

sentences.text:
The "deduction for development"
consists of two components.
The first is with reference to the area required to be utilised for developmental works and the second is the cost of the development works.

Therefore the deduction for the 'development factor' to be made with reference to the price of a small plot in a developed layout, to arrive at the cost of undeveloped land, will be for more than the deduction with reference to the price of a small plot in an unauthorised private layout or an industrial layout.
7. In the present case the land has been acquired for construction of Omkareshwar Canal.
So the amount of expenses that could be incurred in developing the area for construction of canal also varies.
Much more is required to be done for development purposes.
No planned development is required, no internal roads, drainage, sewer, water, electricity lines is required to be developed.
For these reasons the cost of development would be maximum 1/3rd .
The deduction of 65% towards development charges by the learned Reference Court is on higher side.

The reference court reduced the amount of compensation by mechanically applying the formula of deduction of 65%, without considering the fact that land in question was acquired for construction of a canal.

8. On due consideration of the aforesaid, so also in absence of any material, I in the light of para 16 of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sabhia Mohammed Yusuf Abdul Hamid Mulla (dead) by LRs. & Others V/s. Special Land Acquisition Officer & Others (supra), direct the respondents to deduct 1/3rd towards development charges."

15. This Court has already discussed that for the construction of the - : 28 :-

canal, no planned development is required, and no internal road, drainage, water,
electricity, sewer, etc. are required to be developed.
Therefore, the cost of development would be a maximum one one-third and not 65%.
This Court has relied on the judgment of the apex Court in the case of Sabhia Mohammed Yusuf Abdul Hamid Mulla through LRs. V/s. Special Land Acquisition Officer: 2012 (4) MPLJ 589.

24 applied.

Since the landowners have agreed to dispose of their first appeals by accepting one-third deduction as has been granted in the case of Devdutt (supra),
therefore, in the present appeals also, the same deduction is liable to be applied.
In view of the above, no interference with the impugned award passed by the learned Additional District Judge is called for and the appeals are liable to be partly allowed.

16. In view of the above discussion, all the first appeals stand partly allowed while affirming the award of Rs.8.00 Lakhs per Hectare as compensation for irrigated land with a one-third deduction towards development.
17. The review petitions are dismissed as this Court finds no mistake apparent on the face of the record.

It is settled law
that the consent given by the lawyer is not binding on the parties if it is contrary to the facts and law.
Therefore, even if the order/judgment dated 11.5.2020 has been passed with the consent of the Government Advocate and if it is not in accordance with the law and there is a - : 25 :-

review petitions are filed, were decided on the very first day of their listing, without the records of the reference court and the Land Acquisition Officer.

In these present cases, the acquired land in question is situated in Village Pandhranya needed for the completion of the third phase of the canal of the Omkareshwar Project.
All these villages viz. Guljhari, Dhamnod, Vikhron,
Pandhranya and Gyaspur Khedi are adjacent to each other and the purpose of the acquisition order dated the land is the same i.e. construction of the canal, hence the sale-deed of the nearby village can be taken as an exemplar because all the lands are agricultural and are going to get the benefit of irrigation from the water in the canal.
Therefore, the learned Additional District Judge has not committed any error while taking into consideration the sale deeds of a nearby village when no sale deeds were available of the Village Pandhranya.
13.
This Court has relied on the judgment of the apex Court in the case of Sabhia Mohammed Yusuf Abdul Hamid Mulla through LRs. V/s. Special Land Acquisition Officer: 2012 (4) MPLJ 589.
Therefore, in the present case also, the one-third deduction would be permissible.
However, the learned Additional District Judge has not granted any deduction in this case towards development charges which is to be mandatorily Sardar Sarovar Project vs Kalu on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4642154/
24 applied.
